summary: Client physics streaming: the loaded physics of a cluster (physics twin of ls::ClusterVisualLoadedComponent, layouts\alive\ls.ClusterVisualLoadedComponent.json, same size 0xB8 and same member shapes). Written by ls::ClusterLoadHelper<ls::ClusterPhysicsLoaderSystem::LoadOps>::ProcessClusterLoadResult / ProcessContentChanges and ClusterPhysicsLoaderSystem::ApplyLoadResultToEntity (Toolkit GameEngine.dll+0x120E90, +0x11D680); read by phx::PhysXDisableSimulationSystem and phx::PhysXSceneAttacherSystem. macOS names RemoveEntityFromCluster<ls::ClusterPhysicsData, ClusterPhysicsContentComponent, ClusterPhysicsLoadedComponent>. Seen alive on cluster entities of idle levels.

fields.name: Data
fields.evidence: macOS ~ClusterPhysicsLoadedComponent: HashTable<ls::ID<EntityHandleTraits>, HashTableOpsDefault>::~HashTable(this) and frees the values at +0x30 - entity-handle keys. Values are 8-byte ls::ClusterPhysicsData (IndexedStorage<ls::ClusterPhysicsData> with stride 8 in GameEngine.dll+0x110640; Toolkit ProcessClusterLoadResult GameEngine.dll+0x120E90 writes '*(+0x30 + idx*8) = *loadResultData'), written as void* like the visual twin's values (opaque handle/pointer). Windows creator bg3.exe+0x3E77300 zeroes the map, destructor bg3.exe+0x3B714C0 destroys the key set (bg3.exe+0x582AD0) and frees the value buffer at +0x30.

fields.name: Versions
fields.evidence: macOS destructor: HashTable<ID<EntityHandleTraits>> at +0x40, values freed at +0x70. Toolkit GameEngine.dll+0x120E90 inserts into +0x40 (GameEngine.dll+0xED330) and stores a uint32 per key in the value storage at +0x70 (IndexedStorage<unsigned int, s_TagHashTable>, stride 4), keeping the larger of the stored and the new load result's counter (puVar14[2]) - name inferred from that max-update. Windows destructor frees +0x70 and destroys the set at +0x40.

fields.name: Frame
fields.evidence: Toolkit GameEngine.dll+0x1158E0 compares *(int*)(this+0x80) with the frame index (param_2+0x10), stores the new one and clears the ModifiedPair list (+0x94 size). Live: frame-counter-like values.

fields.name: _Pad84
fields.evidence: alignment before the 8-byte aligned array at +0x88; not written (live garbage).

fields.name: ModifiedPairs
fields.evidence: Array of ls::ClusterPhysicsLoadedComponent::ModifiedPair (16-byte elements, Toolkit realloc GameEngine.dll+0x126630 uses count << 4; cleared each frame by GameEngine.dll+0x1158E0; destroyed by GameEngine.dll+0x10EB90 / Windows bg3.exe+0x3B714C0 at +0x88).

fields.name: Added
fields.evidence: Toolkit GameEngine.dll+0x120E90 pushes the load result's 8-byte ls::ClusterPhysicsData here (GameEngine.dll+0x110640(this+0x98, ...), IndexedStorage<ls::ClusterPhysicsData>, stride 8) when a key is new. Windows destructor frees +0x98.

open_questions: What ls::ClusterPhysicsData (8 bytes) holds - written as void*; the uint32 values of the second map are a load counter by their max-update, not named by the game.

fields.name: Entity

fields.name: Data
fields.evidence: Same append: the 8-byte ls::ClusterPhysicsData value the Data map held for that entity (*local_11e0, from GameEngine.dll+0x11B7D0(map+0x30, idx)).

second_pass: macOS destructor names both maps' entity keys, the Toolkit cluster physics loader (GameEngine.dll+0x120E90, +0x1217C0, +0x1158E0; no strings in this layout, so Toolkit and Windows offsets agree with the Windows destructor bg3.exe+0x3B714C0) gives the value widths (8-byte ClusterPhysicsData, uint32), the frame stamp and the 16-byte ModifiedPair {entity, old data}; +0x84 is padding.
